temples.name: Brihadisvara Temple (Peruvudaiyar Kovil)
temples.shortDescription: The Great Living Chola Temple built by Rajaraja Chola I, featuring a 216-foot granite Vimana and monumental stone carvings.
temples.description: A marvel of granite engineering and classical Dravidian proportion, the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur was consecrated by Rajaraja Chola I in 1010 CE. The entire temple is built of hard granite transported from quarries over 50 km away. The towering 13-tiered Vimana (sanctum tower) reaches 66 meters, crowned by an 80-tonne monolithic granite Kumbham (dome).
notableSculptures: Nataraja and Tripurantaka multi-armed bronze and granite sculptures
Eighty-one dance karanas sculpted in low relief along the upper tier corridor
Monumental monolithic Nandi bull measuring 6 meters long and 3.7 meters high
Colossal Dvarapala guardian figures flanking the sanctum entrance
temples.heritageStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site ('Great Living Chola Temples')
temples.historicalReferences: Inscriptions on temple plinth recording endowments, names of 400 court dancers, sculptors, and musicians.
temples.visitingInfo: Open 6:00 AM - 12:30 PM, 4:00 PM - 8:30 PM. Footwear prohibited within inner prakaram.

temples.name: Chennakeshava Temple
temples.shortDescription: Masterpiece of Hoysala architecture famed for its 42 intricate chlorite schist Madanika bracket figures and star-shaped plinth.
temples.description: Commissioned by Hoysala King Vishnuvardhana following his conversion from Jainism to Vaishnavism under Saint Ramanujacharya and victory over the Cholas at Talakadu. Built on a raised stellate (star-shaped) platform (Jagati), the temple exterior features horizontal friezes of thousands of elephants, lions, cavalry, floral scrolls, and epic narratives, surmounted by the world-famous bracket dancers.
notableSculptures: 42 exquisite Madanika bracket sculptures depicting dancing, singing, and toilet scenes
Intricately pierced stone lattice windows (Jali) filtering light into the navaranga hall
Ceiling medallions depicting Narasimha slaying Hiranyakashipu
Sculptor signature inscriptions by renowned master Ruvari Mallitamma and Dasoja
temples.heritageStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site ('Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas', 2023)
temples.historicalReferences: Inscriptions of King Vishnuvardhana (Epigraphia Carnatica Vol. V).
temples.visitingInfo: Open 7:30 AM - 6:30 PM. Guides available at entrance under Karnataka Tourism.

temples.name: Group of Monuments at Mamallapuram
temples.period: 7th – 8th Century CE (Reigns of Mahendravarman I, Narasimhavarman I & Rajasimha)
temples.shortDescription: Historic coastal sanctuary featuring open-air rock bas-reliefs, monolithic Rathas, and the iconic seaside Shore Temple.
temples.description: The maritime capital of the Pallava dynasty showcases the evolution of Indian temple architecture from rock-cut cave shrines (Mandapas) and free-standing monolithic chariot temples (Pancha Rathas) to structural masonry temples (Shore Temple). The granite sculptures celebrate divine communion with nature and the cosmic sea.
notableSculptures: Descent of the Ganga (Arjuna's Penance) colossal open-air bas-relief
Pancha Rathas monolithic models depicting Draupadi, Arjuna, Bhima, Dharmaraja, and Nakula-Sahadeva
Mahishasuramardini Cave relief depicting Goddess Durga charging atop her lion against the buffalo demon
Krishna Butterball balancing monolithic granite boulder
temples.historicalReferences: Pallava royal inscriptions in Grantha and Pallava script praising royal titles (Birudas).
temples.visitingInfo: Open sunrise to sunset (6:00 AM - 6:00 PM). Combined ASI ticketing available.

temples.name: Kailasa Temple (Cave 16), Ellora
temples.period: 8th Century CE (c. 756–774 CE, King Krishna I)
temples.shortDescription: The world's largest monolithic rock excavation, carved top-to-bottom from a single basalt cliff face.
temples.description: Engineered with astonishing mathematical precision, ancient Rashtrakuta artisans excavated 200,000 tonnes of basalt volcanic rock, starting from the summit of the hill downward without scaffolding. The two-story temple complex features life-size elephant statues, soaring victory pillars (Dhvajastambhas), and multi-tiered sculpted galleries.
notableSculptures: Ravana Shaking Mount Kailasa high-relief sculpture on south plinth
Mahabharata and Ramayana epic narrative relief friezes along the base terraces
Life-sized monolithic elephants guarding the courtyard arcade
Gaja-Lakshmi receiving abhishekam at the monumental entrance threshold
temples.historicalReferences: Baroda copper plate inscription of Karka II (c. 812 CE): 'The gods riding in sky chariots were astonished seeing this temple, saying: this is not made by mortal hands.'

temples.name: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple
temples.shortDescription: The crowning achievement of Chandela Nagara architecture, with an 84-miniature-spire Shikhara evoking the peaks of Mount Meru.
temples.description: Rising 31 meters above a high terrace (Adhisthana), Kandariya Mahadeva features over 870 intricately sculpted figures carved into fine buff-colored sandstone. The temple shikhara resembles a cosmic mountain range, with successive miniature spires (Urushringas) clustering around the main central spire in rhythmic ascension.
notableSculptures: Surasundaris and Apsaras applying eye kohl, writing letters, and untying anklets
Mithuna and dynamic erotic-mystical relief panels celebrating divine non-duality and fertility
Dikpalas (Guardians of the Directions) wielding their classical weapons on outer corner buttresses
Intricate geometric ceiling rosettes inside the Mahamandapa
temples.heritageStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Khajuraho Group of Monuments, 1986)
temples.historicalReferences: Chandela dynastic inscriptions recording the patron King Vidyadhara.
temples.visitingInfo: Open sunrise to sunset. Western group audio guides available.

temples.name: Sun Temple at Konark (Black Pagoda)
temples.period: 13th Century CE (c. 1250 CE, King Narasimhadeva I)
temples.shortDescription: Monumental stone chariot of the Sun God with 24 giant sundial wheels and galloping stone horses.
temples.description: Conceived as a colossal stone chariot of Surya, Konark's surviving Jagamohana (assembly hall) and Natamandapa stand as an architectural tour de force on the Bay of Bengal coast. The 24 intricately carved wheels act as precise astronomical sundials measuring hours, sub-hours, and moon phases.
notableSculptures: Three life-sized green chlorite statues of Surya positioned to catch sunrise, noon, and sunset light
24 monolithic chariot wheels with intricate spoke medallions depicting daily rituals and deities
Dynamic Natamandapa musician maidens playing cymbals, drums, flutes, and vinas
Gaja-Simha colossal guardian statues of lions crushing elephants
temples.historicalReferences: Baya Chakada temple palm-leaf chronicle recording construction accounting and chief architect Bisu Maharana.
temples.visitingInfo: Open 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM. Sound and light show in evening.

temples.name: Vittala Temple, Hampi
temples.period: 16th Century CE (Reign of Krishnadevaraya and Achyuta Raya)
temples.shortDescription: The pinnacle of Vijayanagara artistic grandeur, renowned for its monolithic Stone Chariot and musical pillars.
temples.description: Situated along the Tungabhadra river, the Vittala complex represents the culmination of medieval South Indian architectural virtuosity. Its sprawling Ranga Mandapa features 56 monolithic musical pillars (SaReGaMa pillars) engineered to resonate distinct tonal frequencies when gently struck.
notableSculptures: The world-renowned Stone Chariot (Garuda shrine) with revolving granite wheels
Rearing Yali and armed equestrian monoliths supporting high mandapa ceilings
Carved relief panels of foreign Portuguese horse merchants, court ambassadors, and royal dancers
Lotus petal hanging brackets and multifaceted decorative corbels
temples.heritageStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Group of Monuments at Hampi, 1986)
temples.historicalReferences: Chronicles of Portuguese travelers Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz admiring the imperial market and temple festivals.
temples.visitingInfo: Open 8:30 AM - 5:30 PM. Battery-operated eco-buggies available from entrance.

temples.name: Ramappa (Ramalingeswara) Temple
temples.shortDescription: UNESCO World Heritage gem in Telangana, built with buoyant floating bricks and lustrous mirror-polished dolerite bracket figures.
temples.description: Standing on a 6-foot star-shaped cruciform plinth in rural Telangana, the temple is an engineering marvel. It utilized lightweight floating bricks so porous that they float on water, reducing seismic load on the foundation. Its black dolerite bracket dancers possess a lustrous mirror polish that remains unblemished after eight centuries.
notableSculptures: 12 slender dolerite bracket Madanikas with athletic dance poses and high-gloss polish
Nandi bull statue seated alertly, sculpted so that its eyes appear to follow observers from any angle
Exquisite pillar carvings depicting scenes from the Shiva Purana and Jayapa Senani's dance treatise Nritta Ratnavali
Perforated screen stone windows with geometric jali patterns
temples.historicalReferences: Temple inscription dated 1213 CE detailing General Recharla Rudra's dedication to Lord Rudreswara.
temples.visitingInfo: Open 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM daily. Located 70 km from Warangal.
